title: Charlie Parker, Ellington and Freddy Webster as influences
summary: Parker seemed simpler than Ellington to him, so his own music differed from bebop; he admired Freddy Webster's big sound.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Having my ears come from Ellington, Charlie Parker. (Inaudible) I thought Charlie Parker's 2nd Bird was simpler, simpler to hear than Ellington, simpler than Art Tatum. I felt that guys who hadn't heard Duke Ellington, all the beboppers, for instance, or Art Tatum, would think that Charlie Parker was the most complicated, the most advanced lyrical lines going blowing in jazz. I never thought that.

That's the reason why the music I was playing was so different from Charlie Parker. Everybody else was playing bebop. Because I still thought there was something more important than just playing or writing tunes on the blues or some other tune with a different melody. Although Bird did play some hard (inaudible) compositions, I felt it was better if he wrote his own compositions, chord structure and all. Which most of the time he didn't. If he did do that, he did it to a blues structure. Which (inaudible) nobody, he has (inaudible) on the blues.

I liked Bird, but I don't think he influenced me that much. I was influenced by Ellington. Freddy Webster, I liked Freddy Webster's Pass the Barrel, although some people say that Pass the Barrel came from Bird. But according to Fats, Freddy Webster was already playing those type of lines that Bird was playing, before Bird was even heard of. (Singing.)
Which is not bebop, but that was the kind of lines I liked. Freddy playing with Jimmy Nelson's band. His sound was so big. He used to play the ballad Stardust. Little kids in the audience

who didn't know nothing about music, crying. Tears were in their eyes. Of course, mine was flowing, too. So I guess [one of] Freddy Webster (inaudible) on my influence, but I admired his playing and style of playing, especially since he's got such a beautiful sound, and so soulful.
